claims.text: Refractory materials can have extremely high melting temperatures.
A machine-learning interatomic potential trained on DFT data can accurately predict melting properties of high-melting refractory materials.
Direct-coexistence molecular dynamics can determine melting temperature, entropy of fusion, enthalpy of fusion, and volume change at melting.
The ML-based direct-coexistence framework has dramatically lower computational cost than traditional ab initio free-energy methods.
The initial material is a refractory solid near its melting regime.
The proposed intervention trains an ML interatomic potential on high-fidelity DFT calculations.
The proposed intervention uses direct-coexistence MD containing both solid and liquid phases.
The simulation is performed at elevated temperatures near the melting point under solid-liquid coexistence conditions.
The ML potential can encode interatomic interactions accurately across the solid-liquid interface.
The ML potential replicates DFT-level forces at reduced computational cost.
Reduced force-evaluation cost enables sufficiently long MD simulations to capture phase coexistence.
Atomic-scale phase-coexistence evolution permits extraction of the melting temperature and associated fusion properties.
The predicted melting properties will closely approximate DFT predictions.
The computational efficiency of the framework will enable high-throughput melting-property calculations.
Traditional DFT-based ab initio free-energy methods using thermodynamic integration are computationally expensive and poorly suited to high-throughput analysis.
Accuracy depends on the quality and transferability of the ML potential, including its coverage of composition and extreme thermodynamic conditions.
Insufficient training coverage can cause deviations from DFT-level accuracy.
Prediction errors depend on training quality, phase-space coverage, and simulation timescale.
